title: PTStore (Prefix Tensor Store): Distributed Prefix Caching and Replication for High Throughput Inference Serving
event_hint: PTStore: a distributed prefix caching and replication system that stores reusable KV-cache prefix tensors across nodes/GPUs to accelerate LLM inference, from JHU and Argonne.
problem: Existing inference runtimes (vLLM, DeepSpeed-MII, LMCache, Mooncake, SGLang) cache KV results mostly in local GPU/host memory; they lack support for aggregating distributed memory tiers, so cross-node prefix reuse requires regenerating the KV cache, causing load imbalance when popular tensors concentrate on a few servers and capping total KV-cache capacity.
mechanism: Inspired by CDN client-caching, PTStore distributes and replicates popular tensors that form reusable KV-cache prefixes across distributed nodes and GPUs. It uses incremental tensor storage to minimize redundancy, consolidated metadata for rapid longest-common-prefix (LCP) queries, and a replication strategy optimizing local access to hot prefixes. Clients issue LCP queries (broadcast+reduce) and read/write tensor subsets via optimized RDMA built on the Mochi composable stack (Thallium C++ wrapper over Mercury and Argobots), progressing multiple servers in parallel. It integrates with existing LLM runtimes (e.g., vLLM).

evidence.claim: PTStore executes inferences on long-passage Q&A datasets 5-6 times more efficiently than current baselines that do not aggregate memory across nodes/GPUs and therefore regenerate the KV cache.
evidence.baseline: baselines that do not aggregate memory across nodes/GPUs (require KV cache regeneration)

evidence.claim: In TTFT scalability tests (1k-8k tokens, vLLM, SQUAD), PTStore outperforms vLLM's prefix caching starting at 2k tokens and is almost 2x faster at 8k tokens.
evidence.condition: vLLM runtime, SQUAD dataset, 8k token sequences, TTFT metric

evidence.claim: PTStore is more than 2x faster than EvoStore for 1k-token sequences and about 20% faster for 8k tokens, with the advantage attributed to prefix replication (Fig.4b I/O vs compute breakdown).
evidence.condition: TTFT, SQUAD dataset, 1k and 8k token sequences

evidence.claim: Experimental evaluations show PTStore significantly reduces Time to First Token (TTFT) versus state of the art by up to an order of magnitude and remains scalable across variable sequence lengths.
evidence.value: up to an order of magnitude

evidence.claim: Workloads use WikiQA (3,000 questions, page lengths 2,000-40,000 tokens) for scaling experiments and SQUAD (100,000 questions) for reading-comprehension extractive tasks; both are long-prompt/short-answer workloads that stress the prefill stage.

evaluation_context: Research prototype (JHU + Argonne) evaluated on extractive long-context Q&A (WikiQA, SQUAD). Communication uses optimized bulk RDMA via Mochi/Thallium. Reported metrics focus on TTFT and end-to-end runtime; sequence lengths tested 1k-8k tokens. No TPOT, token throughput, network utilization, or end-to-end P95 latency numbers are visible in the Evidence Pack; no production hardware spec or deployment scale (node/GPU counts) is exposed.
limitations: TTFT and end-to-end runtime are the main reported metrics; decode-phase (TPOT), token throughput, and P95 latency are not reported in the visible evidence. Hardware platform, exact node/GPU counts, and RDMA fabric specs are not exposed. Results are specific to extractive long-context Q&A workloads (long prompt, short answer) which favor prefill optimization; performance on short prompts or decode-heavy chat workloads is not characterized. For small query lengths vLLM's baseline prefix caching is superior, per the authors.
project_relevance: PTStore is a distributed prefix-cache storage layer using RDMA for cross-node KV-cache access, directly relevant to KVCache-aware network/bandwidth scheduling and the TPN question of whether network-side mechanisms reduce cross-node KVCache transfer and improve TTFT. It offers a concrete reference point for how distributed KV-cache aggregation changes the storage/network boundary, though it is a research prototype, not an Alibaba TPN product.
source_notes: arXiv preprint 2607.22648v1 (25 Jun 2026), FETCHED primary source.
Headline 5-6x efficiency gain is an abstract claim whose detailed baseline and workload condition are restated but the exact measurement table is in the unread suffix.
Comparison baselines are explicitly named: vLLM (prefix caching), EvoStore; related systems discussed include LMCache, Mooncake, SGLang (RadixAttention), Splitwise, DistServe.
